elements.content: Communication Goal: I can talk about amounts, prices and what is too expensive when shopping.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A2 General English
- Unit: Unit 11. Shopping
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: holiday shopping
- Materials: COSYmanuals A2 pages for Much, Many, Little, Few, Too and Enough, whiteboard, coursebook, audio player, timer.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• I can talk about amounts, prices and what is too expensive when shopping.
• use Much, Many, Little, Few, Too and Enough accurately in context
• use the target vocabulary and chunks in a discussion

teacher_notes.title: Lesson metadata
teacher_notes.content: Level: A2 | Unit: Unit 11. Shopping | Mode: individual / pair / group | Duration options: 60 / 90 / 120 min.

teacher_notes.title: Communication goal
teacher_notes.content: I can talk about amounts, prices and what is too expensive when shopping.

teacher_notes.title: Lead-in discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask the class: Do holidays make us spend too much? Give students two minutes in pairs, then take three answers. Do not correct language yet; note useful vocabulary on the board.

teacher_notes.title: Goal discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'What can you already do in English connected to holiday shopping? What do you want to be able to do by the end of the lesson?' Write two answers on the board.

teacher_notes.title: Success criteria
teacher_notes.content: Learners can complete the speaking task with at least five target words and the target grammar with reasonable accuracy.

teacher_notes.title: Fast finisher
teacher_notes.content: Ask early finishers to add two more questions about holiday shopping for the class.

teacher_notes.title: Bridging question
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'What do you already know about holiday shopping? What would you like to learn today?'

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

gift — a present.
receipt — a piece of paper proving you paid.
sale — a period when shops sell things cheaply.
bargain /ˈbɑː.ɡɪn/ — something bought for less than its usual price.
queue /kjuː/ — a line of people waiting.
budget /ˈbʌdʒɪt/ — a plan for how much money you can spend.
discount — money taken off the usual price.
checkout /ˈtʃek.aʊt/ — the place where you pay in a shop.
stressful /ˈstres.fəl/ — Causing feelings of worry and tension. Example: Moving to a new house is stressful.
list /lɪst/ — To make a itemized record or catalogue of items. Example: Please list all references used in your research assignment.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Where is the fitting room?
• Can I return this if it doesn't fit?
• Keep the receipt for an exchange
• Is this dress on sale?
• Do you have this in a larger size?
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the place where you pay in a shop'?
Which word means 'To make a itemized record or catalogue of items'?
Which word means 'a line of people waiting'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.placeholder: Complete: Holiday shopping can be stressful.

teacher_notes.title: 5-step vocabulary progression
teacher_notes.content: 1 Recognition -> 2 Pronunciation -> 3 Matching/classification -> 4 Controlled production -> 5 Personalised use. Keep the pace brisk and check meaning before form.

teacher_notes.title: Meaning check
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which word means ...?' Use the definitions on the slide. Then ask students to cover the definitions and explain three words in their own words.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: Do you enjoy shopping for gifts? Encourage students to use at least three target words in their answers.

teacher_notes.title: Anticipated problems
teacher_notes.content: Watch for pronunciation problems in gift, receipt, sale. Drill the words chorally and individually before the practice.

teacher_notes.title: Extension
teacher_notes.content: Ask students to categorise the ten words into 'people', 'actions' and 'things', then compare categories with a partner.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus: 'much' /mʌtʃ/ and 'many' /ˈmeni/; weak 'enough' /ɪˈnʌf/.

Target words: gift, receipt, sale
Stress and IPA: listen to the model, mark the stressed syllable, then repeat.
Listen and repeat:
Where is the fitting room? Can I return this if it doesn't fit? Keep the receipt for an exchange
Mark the stressed syllable in these words:

elements.placeholder: Mark the stress: gift, receipt, sale

teacher_notes.title: Pronunciation aim
teacher_notes.content: 'much' /mʌtʃ/ and 'many' /ˈmeni/; weak 'enough' /ɪˈnʌf/.

teacher_notes.title: Drill script
teacher_notes.content: Model each word twice. Use choral repetition, then individual repetition. Ask students to tap the stressed syllable. Finish with the sentence drill: 'Where is the fitting room?'.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which words are difficult for you? Why?' Let students compare first language sounds with English sounds.

teacher_notes.title: Peer discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask pairs to choose the two hardest words and agree on one tip for saying them. Take two tips from the class.

teacher_notes.title: Error correction
teacher_notes.content: Correct only the target feature during the drill. Note other errors for delayed feedback at the end of the lesson.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: use Much, Many, Little, Few, Too and Enough to talk about holiday shopping.

Form:
much + uncountable nouns; many + countable nouns.
a little + uncountable; a few + countable.

too + adjective/adverb (more than we want).
adjective/adverb + enough (the right amount).
too much / too many + noun.

Examples:
• I don't have much time, but I have a few ideas.
• There are many shops but little parking.
• The flat is too expensive for us.
• She isn't old enough to drive.
Controlled practice: check the meaning and form.
Is 'many' for countable nouns?
Is 'a little' for uncountable nouns?
Does 'too' mean more than is good?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I don't have much time, but I have a few ideas.
• Now change the subject and the time.
• Now make a question.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Do holidays make us spend too much?
• Do you enjoy shopping for gifts?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences on the topic 'holiday shopping' using the target structure.
• Write one question to ask your partner.

teacher_notes.title: Function-first grammar rule
teacher_notes.content: Frame the grammar as a communicative tool, not an abstract rule: Much, Many, Little, Few, Too and Enough helps learners talk about holiday shopping.

teacher_notes.title: CCQs
teacher_notes.content: Is 'many' for countable nouns? (Yes.) Is 'a little' for uncountable nouns? (Yes.)

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: How can you save money at holidays? Push students to justify their answers with a full sentence using the target grammar.

teacher_notes.title: Common errors
teacher_notes.content: 'many money' -> 'much money'. 'a few water' -> 'a little water'. 'enough big' -> 'big enough'.

teacher_notes.title: Extension
teacher_notes.content: Ask students to transform two sentences into a question and a negative, then check with a partner.

elements.content: Reading: Holiday shopping

Holiday shopping can be stressful. There are too many people in the shops and too little time. 'I buy a few gifts online,' says Nina. 'It is cheaper, and I don't have to carry heavy bags.' She starts early and makes a list.
Holiday shopping can be ___.
'It is cheaper, and I don't have to carry heavy bags.' She starts early and makes a ___.
What is the text mainly about?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Excuse me, where is the fitting room? I'd like to try on these jeans.
B: They are right past the cash registers on your left.
A: Thanks! If they don't fit, can I exchange them?
B: Yes, within 30 days as long as you keep the receipt.
B: Yes, within 30 days as long as you keep the ___.

teacher_notes.title: Skills focus
teacher_notes.content: Listening (~10%) + Reading (~10%). The reading gives context; the dialogue models the target chunks in a real exchange.

teacher_notes.title: Pre-reading discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: Is online shopping better at Christmas? Set a purpose for reading: 'Read to find out what the person says about holiday shopping.'

teacher_notes.title: Comprehension check
teacher_notes.content: Students answer alone, then compare in pairs. Check answers with the whole class and ask students to justify them from the text.

teacher_notes.title: Post-reading discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Do you agree with the person in the text? Why or why not?' Use the target vocabulary in the discussion.

elements.content: Speaking task: discuss the topic 'holiday shopping' with your partner. Use at least five target words and the target grammar.

• Do holidays make us spend too much?
• Do you enjoy shopping for gifts?
• How can you save money at holidays?
• Is online shopping better at Christmas?
Adult speaking frames:

• I don't have much ... / many ...
• There are only a few ... left.
• I have too much ... and not enough ...
Role-play card: Do holidays make us spend too much?

Student A: You have a strong view on 'Do holidays make us spend too much?'. Explain your opinion with two reasons and one example from your own life.

Student B: You partly disagree. Ask one follow-up question, then give a different view using the target language.

Swap roles after four minutes.
Writing task: write a short message (60-80 words) to a friend or colleague about 'holiday shopping'. Use the target grammar and at least five target words.
Model: Holiday shopping can be stressful. There are too many people in the shops and too little time. Use the target grammar and at least five target words.
Peer check: swap your message with a partner. Underline one sentence you like and one verb form to check. Then ask one spoken question about your partner's text.

teacher_notes.title: Speaking aim (~70%)
teacher_notes.content: Fluency first, accuracy second. Give students 6-8 minutes for the pair task, then ask two pairs to report back.

teacher_notes.title: Monitoring focus
teacher_notes.content: Monitor for the target grammar and the ten target words. Note three good sentences and three errors for delayed feedback.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask the class: 'Do holidays make us spend too much?' and 'Do you enjoy shopping for gifts?' Encourage students to respond to each other, not just to you.

teacher_notes.title: Feedback discussion
teacher_notes.content: After the role-play, ask: 'Which question produced the most interesting answer? Why?' Invite two pairs to share one answer with the class.

teacher_notes.title: Speaking frames discussion
teacher_notes.content: Put the three frames on the board. Ask students which frame is most useful for their own life and why. Drill the frames chorally, then let students personalise them.

teacher_notes.title: Role-play setup
teacher_notes.content: Assign A and B. Give A one minute to prepare two reasons. Give B one minute to prepare one question and a different view. Monitor for the target grammar and the ten target words.

teacher_notes.title: Writing support
teacher_notes.content: Give students 6 minutes to write 60-80 words. Remind them to use the model, the frames, and at least five target words.

teacher_notes.title: Peer-check discussion
teacher_notes.content: Pairs swap messages, underline one strong sentence and one verb form to check, then ask one spoken question about the text. Take two examples of good language from the class.

teacher_notes.title: Extension
teacher_notes.content: Ask fast finishers to turn their message into a short spoken update and deliver it to another pair.

elements.content: Timestamped Multi-Duration Flows:

• 60 min (Essential): 0-8 Warm-up & goal; 8-18 Vocabulary & chunks; 18-28 Grammar & controlled practice; 28-40 Reading/listening + speaking; 40-50 Role-play; 50-60 Cool-down & homework.

• 90 min (Expanded): 0-10 Warm-up; 10-25 Vocabulary & pronunciation; 25-40 Grammar & controlled practice; 40-55 Reading/listening; 55-70 Speaking task; 70-85 Writing & feedback; 85-90 Cool-down.

• 120 min (Full Workshop): 0-15 Warm-up & discussion; 15-35 Vocabulary & pronunciation lab; 35-60 Grammar workshop; 60-80 Reading/listening & language focus; 80-100 Speaking role-play; 100-115 Writing & portfolio; 115-120 Feedback & homework.

teacher_notes.title: Multi-duration strategy
teacher_notes.content: Choose the 60, 90 or 120-minute flow before the lesson. The core is the same; the expanded versions add practice and feedback, not new grammar.

teacher_notes.title: Timing discussion
teacher_notes.content: If time is short, cut the writing task to two sentences and keep the speaking task. If time is long, add the extension on slide 7.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which part of this lesson do you need most practice in: vocabulary, grammar or speaking?' Use the answer to choose the longer flow.

teacher_notes.title: Planning note
teacher_notes.content: The 60-minute flow is the minimum for a complete lesson. Do not skip the recycling or the speaking task; they carry the communicative goal.
